NDT training in Portland: how it works for Portland employers and technicians

NDT training in Portland, Oregon is delivered by Atlantis NDT as ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III courses in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET, taught live online or onsite at your shipyard, mill, fabrication shop or plant under ASNT Level III oversight. Your employer certifies you under its written practice after training hours, documented experience, general, specific and practical exams, and a vision test.

Portland's NDT market is less obvious than a Gulf Coast refinery town, but it is broad. Ship repair on Swan Island, a steel plate mill and rail car builders on the Willamette and Columbia, aerospace castings and component manufacturers in the metro area, semiconductor fabs to the west, the fuel tank farms of the Critical Energy Infrastructure Hub along the Willamette in Northwest Portland, dams and hydro on the Columbia, and a long list of bridge projects, from the Willamette crossings downtown to the Interstate Bridge Replacement on I-5. Crews here also work across the river in Vancouver, Washington, so many Portland technicians operate in two states.

Atlantis NDT does not run a Portland classroom. We serve Portland employers and technicians by delivering theory live online and bringing practical training, exams and Level III documentation to your facility. This section adds the depth the overview above does not: a method-by-method map to Portland work, the certification path in order, scheduling around dry-dock and construction seasons, Oregon and Washington radiation licensing, and an honest note on aerospace work. Request a Portland training quote; we usually reply within one business day.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Portland

Each course follows the SNT-TC-1A body of knowledge for the method and level and is aligned to the codes your Portland work falls under.

MethodLevelsWhat Portland employers use it forPrerequisite
Ultrasonic testing (UT)I, II, III prepHull and structural weld inspection in ship repair, plate inspection at the mill, thickness surveys on fuel tanks and piping, bridge welds and pinsLevel I: employer entry rules. Level II: Level I plus documented experience
Phased array UT (PAUT)II, III prepEncoded weld inspection on heavy fabrication and bridges, corrosion mapping on tanks and terminal piping, penstock and hydro component weldsConventional UT Level II expected first
Time-of-flight diffraction (TOFD)II, III prepThrough-wall sizing on thick plate and heavy structural weldsConventional UT Level II expected first
Radiographic testing (RT)I, II, III prepPiping welds in fabrication and repair, castings, pipeline tie-insState radiation safety qualification required before working with sources
Magnetic particle testing (MT)I, IIStructural and bridge welds, rail car and truck frame components, ship structure, lifting gearNone for Level I; Level I plus experience for Level II
Liquid penetrant testing (PT)I, IIStainless process piping in semiconductor and food plants, aluminium and non-magnetic parts, castingsNone for Level I; Level I plus experience for Level II
Visual testing (VT)I, IIWeld acceptance across structural, marine and pipe fabrication; tank and structure condition inspection; borescope inspection of high-purity tubingNone for Level I; Level I plus experience for Level II
Eddy current testing (ET)I, IIHeat-exchanger and condenser tubing at power and process plants, surface crack detection through coatingsNone for Level I; Level I plus experience for Level II

UT training covers sound propagation, probe selection, calibration, DAC and TCG, angle-beam weld scanning and flaw evaluation, with practice geared to plate, structural T-joints and marine weld geometry. PAUT and TOFD cover focal laws, scan plans, encoded collection and analysis for technicians already confident in conventional UT, and are increasingly specified on bridge and heavy fabrication work. RT covers exposure technique, image quality, film and digital interpretation and code acceptance. MT is the everyday method for Portland's structural, marine and transportation-equipment work. PT and VT matter for the high-purity piping of the semiconductor sector. ET suits technicians who want plant outage work. Level III candidates prepare for the ASNT Basic and Method exams through ASNT Level III training.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Portland, step by step

Oregon and Washington do not license NDT technicians by method. Your employer certifies you, in this order:

  1. Employer written practice. Sets training and experience hours, exams, grading, vision requirements, recertification intervals and the responsible Level III.
  2. Classroom training. The formal training for your method and level, live online, in an arranged cohort, or onsite. Recommended minimums are in our training requirements matrix.
  3. On-the-job experience. Supervised and documented hours in the method on real work.
  4. General exam. Written questions on method principles.
  5. Specific exam. Written questions on your employer's procedures, equipment and codes, for example AWS D1.1, AWS D1.5, ASME Section V or API 1104.
  6. Practical exam. Hands-on examination of flawed specimens. A Level III administers and grades all three exams.
  7. Vision test. Near-vision acuity and colour contrast, annually.
  8. Certification. Issued by the employer and signed by the Level III.
  9. Recertification. On the interval the written practice sets; a new employer recertifies you under its own practice.

More detail: SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Portland crews

  • Live online theory: instructor-led classroom hours in real time, practical for shop and yard crews on fixed shifts. See online NDT training.
  • Onsite at your facility: theory, practical and exams at your yard, mill, shop or plant, using your equipment and specimens that match your product.
  • Blended: theory online, then an in-person practical and exam block. No credible scheme allows a remote practical exam.

Portland scheduling has its own patterns. Ship repair work follows dry-dock bookings, which can change at short notice when a vessel arrives early or late. Bridge and heavy civil work peaks in the drier months from late spring to early autumn, which makes the wet season the natural window for classroom training of field crews. Plant outages at power and process facilities are planned months ahead. Tell us your calendar. Ask about onsite training for your Portland crew, or see corporate NDT training.

Where NDT technicians work in Portland

Ship repair and marine fabrication. Vigor's Swan Island shipyard, with its large floating dry docks, handles commercial, government and Navy repair and new construction, and marine fabricators along the Willamette and Columbia build barges, ferries and workboats. Navy work falls under NAVSEA technical publications and classed vessels under ABS rules, which add requirements on top of an employer's written practice. VT, MT and UT on hull, deck and piping welds are the core methods.

Steel, rail and heavy transportation equipment. A steel plate mill in the Rivergate industrial area, rail car builders on the Willamette and heavy-truck manufacturing headquartered on Swan Island all generate plate, weld and component inspection. MT and UT dominate, working to AWS D1.1 and customer or industry specifications.

Aerospace castings and components. Portland is home to large aerospace casting and forging operations and component manufacturers, including Boeing's plant in Gresham. Castings are inspected by PT, RT and increasingly CT to customer specifications. We are honest here: aerospace employers usually certify NDT personnel to NAS 410 under Nadcap-audited programmes, and Atlantis does not train to NAS 410. SNT-TC-1A method training builds knowledge that transfers, but those employers certify you under their own scheme.

Fuel terminals and pipelines. The Critical Energy Infrastructure Hub in Northwest Portland holds most of Oregon's liquid fuel supply in tank farms fed by pipeline, barge and rail. Oregon's 2022 legislation requiring seismic vulnerability assessments for large fuel terminals has added engineering and inspection scope. Tank and terminal work uses UT thickness, PAUT corrosion mapping, MT and VT, and pipeline work follows API 1104.

Semiconductors and high-purity manufacturing. Intel's Hillsboro campus and its supply chain build ultra-high-purity gas and chemical systems from orbital-welded stainless tubing, inspected visually and by borescope, with PT where accessible.

Bridges, dams and power. The Willamette River bridges, the Earthquake Ready Burnside Bridge project, the Interstate Bridge Replacement between Portland and Vancouver, and the Columbia River dams all need weld and structure inspection, with steel bridge welding governed by AWS D1.5. Gas-fired power plants in the region, and Washington's Columbia Generating Station farther up the river, bring outage work in UT, ET and VT.

Radiography licensing in Oregon and Washington. Oregon is an NRC Agreement State; radioactive-source industrial radiography is licensed and inspected by the Oregon Health Authority's Radiation Protection Services, and radiographers must meet its radiation safety training and certification rules in addition to SNT-TC-1A certification in RT. Washington is also an Agreement State, regulated by the Washington State Department of Health, so crews working in Vancouver or elsewhere across the Columbia must meet Washington's rules or reciprocity requirements. Our RT courses teach the method; they do not replace radiation safety requirements.

What local employers ask for. Level II in MT and UT is the most common request, VT for fabrication and marine work, and PAUT for bridge and heavy fabrication. Some local employers also ask for AWS CWI, CSWIP, ISO 9712 or NAS 410 certification; Atlantis does not train for those schemes. For pay context, see our NDT salary guide.

Level III services and written practices for Portland NDT companies

Many Portland NDT companies and in-house inspection departments are small, serve both marine and structural customers, and work in two states. A written practice that does not name the codes your customers invoke, or that was copied from another company, fails audits. Atlantis reviews or writes your NDT written practice to the current SNT-TC-1A edition or to CP-189 where customers require it, provides outsourced Level III services for exams, procedure approval and certification, writes method procedures aligned to AWS, ASME or customer specifications, and audits certification files before a customer does. Book a Level III consultation for your Portland company. Background: SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Practise before the practical exam

Practical NDT, our 3D simulator, lets trainees practise 12 methods across five environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. Portland candidates can rehearse weld scanning, yoke placement and set-up sequences between sessions. It is practice only and does not replace the practical exam on real specimens.

Your instructor

Programmes are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, who oversees course content, examinations and Level III sign-off for Atlantis cohorts delivered online and onsite.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Portland

How do I get NDT certified in Portland?

Be hired or sponsored by an employer that performs NDT, complete the training and supervised experience its written practice requires, pass the general, specific and practical exams given by a Level III, and pass a vision test. Your employer then certifies you.

Can I take NDT training online in Oregon?

Yes for the classroom portion, where your employer's written practice accepts live online delivery. The practical training and practical exam are always in person on real specimens.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on the training and experience hours your employer's written practice sets and on how much documented experience you already have. See the training requirements matrix. Supervised experience usually takes longer than the classroom work.

Do I need a license for radiography in Oregon?

To work with radioactive sources, yes: industrial radiography is licensed by the Oregon Health Authority's Radiation Protection Services, and radiographers must meet its radiation safety training and certification rules. That is separate from SNT-TC-1A certification in RT. Work in Washington falls under the Washington State Department of Health.

What does NDT training cost in Portland?

We quote on request, based on method, level, group size, delivery mode and whether exams and Level III support are included. Cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Portland employers?

Yes, across marine, structural, fabrication, terminal and plant work, where SNT-TC-1A is the usual basis for employer certification. Aerospace employers generally certify to NAS 410 instead.

Is this page about Portland, Oregon or Portland, Maine?

Portland, Oregon, and the wider Portland-Vancouver metro area. Onsite delivery is available elsewhere in the US too.

Can I get aerospace NDT certification through Atlantis?

Atlantis trains to SNT-TC-1A only and does not offer NAS 410 training. The method knowledge transfers, but aerospace employers certify you under their own NAS 410 programme.

Which method should I learn first for Portland work?

VT and MT are the fastest routes into marine and structural fabrication work. UT is the method most in demand once you are established, and PAUT is the step up.

Can you train our crew onsite in Portland or Vancouver, Washington?

Yes. Onsite delivery covers both sides of the Columbia and the wider Pacific Northwest.

Do you offer CWI or ISO 9712 training?

No. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based only. Some Portland employers ask for those credentials, which are earned through their own schemes.

Can my company outsource its Level III?

Yes. Ask about outsourced Level III support in Portland.
